answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because prism only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, gale is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any pearl approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
